title: AP CSP — Lesson 10 Homework: Boolean Logic
notice: All questions are original. Q1–Q6 are AP-style practice, not official AP questions. Written tasks and 30 marks are teacher-designed. Q5 earns one mark only for both correct choices and no others. OR is inclusive. Logical operands are Boolean values; age, score and x are numeric. Parentheses specify grouping. The Workshop Rule Checker is a fictional teaching example.

questions.explanation: C is correct: division gives 2.8 and 14 = 2 × 5 + 4. A truncates division. B uses the whole-group count for MOD. D reverses or confuses the two results.
D includes equality. A and C are strict comparisons and fail when the values are equal. B is false because the values are equal.

questions.topic: Retrieval: assignment of a Boolean result
questions.prompt: Trace: score ← 7; passed ← (score ≥ 5); score ← 2. What does passed hold?

options.label: D
options.text: The expression score ≥ 5, which updates automatically

questions.explanation: A is correct: passed stores true when assigned and is never reassigned. B wrongly recalculates after score changes. C confuses two variables. D treats assignment as a live formula.

questions.prompt: booked and hasPass are both true. What is booked OR hasPass?

options.label: A
options.text: false, because exactly one must be true

options.label: B
options.text: true, because OR allows one or both true

questions.explanation: B matches inclusive OR. A describes an exclusive choice, not AP OR. C invents numeric counting. D confuses a Boolean result with a string.

questions.prompt: For Boolean A and B, which TWO statements are true? Select exactly TWO answers.

options.label: A
options.text: true AND false evaluates to true.

options.label: C
options.text: NOT (A OR B) always equals (NOT A) OR (NOT B).

options.label: D
options.text: NOT (A AND B) always equals (NOT A) OR (NOT B).

questions.explanation: B reverses false. D is the correct De Morgan equivalence. A is false because AND needs both true. C needs AND between the negated operands; A=true, B=false is a counterexample.

questions.prompt: Which expression is true exactly when age is from 12 through 17, inclusive?
questions.explanation: C enforces both inclusive bounds. A excludes the endpoints. B accepts out-of-range ages, such as 5. D accepts only the two endpoints, excluding valid interior ages.

questions.prompt:
For score = 20, evaluate each expression.
(a) score > 20   (b) score ≥ 20
(c) score ≠ 20   (d) NOT (score > 20)

rubric.criterion: (a) false.
(b) true.
(c) false.
(d) true.

questions.prompt:
For each row, give A AND B and A OR B, in that order.
(a) A=true, B=true   (b) A=true, B=false
(c) A=false, B=true   (d) A=false, B=false
questions.answer: (a) true, true. (b) false, true. (c) false, true. (d) false, false.
questions.explanation: (a) true, true. (b) false, true. (c) false, true. (d) false, false.

rubric.criterion: Both outputs correct for row (a): true, true.
Both outputs correct for row (b): false, true.
Both outputs correct for row (c): false, true.
Both outputs correct for row (d): false, false.

questions.prompt:
Write a Boolean expression for each condition.
(a) x is at least 4 and at most 9.
(b) x is outside that inclusive range, without using NOT.
Then evaluate expression (a) for (c) x=4 and (d) x=10.

rubric.criterion: Correct inclusive-range expression, or an equivalent expression.
Correct outside-range expression with strict bounds and no NOT.
At x=4 the inclusive-range result is true.
At x=10 the inclusive-range result is false.

questions.prompt:
(a) Rewrite NOT (A AND B) with NOT applied only to individual operands.
(b) Do the same for NOT (A OR B).
For A=false and B=true, evaluate (c) NOT (A AND B) and (d) (NOT A) AND (NOT B).
questions.answer: (a) (NOT A) OR (NOT B). (b) (NOT A) AND (NOT B). (c) true. (d) false; these two expressions are not equivalent.
questions.explanation: (a) (NOT A) OR (NOT B). (b) (NOT A) AND (NOT B). (c) true. (d) false; these two expressions are not equivalent.

rubric.criterion: (a) Both operands negated and joined with OR.
(b) Both operands negated and joined with AND.
(c) true.
(d) false.

questions.prompt: Use inRange ← (age ≥ 12) AND (age ≤ 17), hasEntry ← booked OR hasPass, eligible ← inRange AND hasEntry. For age=14, booked=true, hasPass=true, give (a) inRange, (b) hasEntry, (c) eligible. (d) On a new run with age=18 and the same credentials, give eligible.
questions.answer: (a) true. (b) true. (c) true. (d) false. The new run recomputes the conditions.
questions.explanation: (a) true. (b) true. (c) true. (d) false. The new run recomputes the conditions.

rubric.criterion: (a) inRange is true.
(b) hasEntry is true, including the both-true OR case.
(c) eligible is true.
(d) eligible is false after all conditions are recomputed for age=18.

questions.topic: Repair a range condition and test it
questions.prompt:
Bug: inRange ← (age ≥ 12) OR (age ≤ 17). The intended range is 12–17 inclusive.
(a) Give the buggy result for age=5. (b) Correct the assignment.
For the corrected code give the expected result at (c) age=12 and (d) age=11.

rubric.criterion: Buggy age=5 result is true.
Correct assignment enforces both inclusive bounds with AND, or equivalent logic.
Corrected result at age=12 is true.
Corrected result at age=11 is false.
